subproblem.title: Poincaré and trace inequalities on the unit cube with an integer median (C1–C2)
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, Q₁ := {y ∈ ℝⁿ : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} (Euclid n, Lebesgue measure), and div G := trace of the derivative (LinearMap.trace of fderiv). There is c > 0, depending only on m, such that: if u : ℝⁿ → ℝ is integer-valued (u(y) ∈ ℤ for every y), integrable on Q₁, and V ∈ ℝ satisfies ∫_{Q₁} u·div g ≤ V for every C^∞ map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞), i.e. C^∞, not analytic) with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y, then there is β ∈ ℤ with (1) ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ cV, (2) |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|, and (3) |∫_{Q₁}(u − β)·div G| ≤ cV for every C^∞ map G : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with |G(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ m : ℕ, ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ (u : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (V : ℝ), (∀ y, ∃ z : ℤ, u y = z) → IntegrableOn u {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ g : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, u y * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ g y) ≤ V) → ∃ β : ℤ, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y - β| ≤ c * V ∧ |(β : ℝ)| ≤ 2 * ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y| ∧ ∀ G : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) G → (∀ y, ‖G y‖ ≤ 1) → |∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, (u y - β) * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ G y)| ≤ c * V
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Part C (C1, C2) of the parent proof and its use in step E7(c). C1(i) is conclusion (1) (with the integer median of C2); C2 gives (2); C1(ii) applied to u − β (same V), i.e. the bound on the boundary mass of (u − β)[[Q₁]], is conclusion (3), written without currents: by d(Σ_j G_j ε_j) = (div G) dy (ε_j := (−1)^{j−1}dy¹ ∧ ⋯ ∧ dy^{j−1} ∧ dy^{j+1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dyⁿ), ∂((u − β)[[Q₁]]) tested on the (n − 1)-form with coefficient field G is ∫_{Q₁}(u − β) div G. (In Simon this replaces the BV facts Ch. 6, 2.35–2.37 and Ch. 2, 2.7, 2.9 used in displays (26)–(33) of the proof of 5.1.)

Notation. n := m + 1 ≥ 1, Q₁ := (0,1)ⁿ ⊆ ℝⁿ (Lebesgue measure Lⁿ, Lⁿ(Q₁) = 1), div G := trace DG. L¹ convergence of mollifications, used in 3 and 5: for f ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ), f ∗ φ_σ → f in L¹ as σ ↓ 0 (approximate f in L¹ by v ∈ C_c(ℝⁿ); v ∗ φ_σ → v uniformly with supports in a fixed compact set, and ‖(f − v) ∗ φ_σ‖_{L¹} ≤ ‖f − v‖_{L¹} by Fubini, as φ_σ ≥ 0 has integral 1). For 0 < δ < 1/8, Q_δ := (δ, 1 − δ)ⁿ (side s = 1 − 2δ ∈ [3/4, 1]). φ ∈ C_c^∞(B_1(0)), φ ≥ 0, ∫φ = 1, φ_σ(z) := σ^{−n}φ(z/σ), φ̌_σ(z) := φ_σ(−z). ū := u·1_{Q₁} ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ), u_σ := ū ∗ φ_σ ∈ C^∞(ℝⁿ). Let u, V be as in the statement; "admissible g" means g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ smooth with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g| ≤ 1.

0. Preliminaries. Taking g = 0 gives V ≥ 0. Applying the hypothesis to g and −g gives |∫_{Q₁} u div g| ≤ V for every admissible g (so V bounds the parent's sup V of C1). For every constant β and admissible g, ∫_{Q₁} β div g = 0 (integrate each ∂_i g_i along coordinate lines; g has compact support in Q₁). Hence v := u − β is integrable on Q₁ and satisfies the same hypothesis with the same V.

1. Gradient bound (parent C1, first sentence): for 0 < σ < δ < 1/8, ∫_{Q_δ}|∇u_σ| ≤ V. For g ∈ C_c^∞(Q_δ; ℝⁿ) with |g| ≤ 1, Fubini and differentiation under the convolution give ∫ ∇u_σ · g = −∫ u_σ div g = −∫ ū (φ̌_σ ∗ div g) = −∫_{Q₁} u div(φ̌_σ ∗ g). Here φ̌_σ ∗ g is smooth with compact support in Q_δ + B_σ(0) ⊆ Q₁ and |φ̌_σ ∗ g| ≤ 1, so the right side is ≤ V by 0. The supremum of ∫ ∇u_σ · g over such g equals ∫_{Q_δ}|∇u_σ|: take g_k := χ_k∇u_σ/(|∇u_σ|² + 1/k)^{1/2} with smooth cut-offs 0 ≤ χ_k ≤ 1, χ_k ↑ 1_{Q_δ}, and use monotone convergence.

2. Smooth Poincaré inequality (parent C1). For a cube Q' of side s ∈ [1/2, 1] and v ∈ C¹(closure Q'), ∫_{Q'}|v − v_{Q'}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n∫_{Q'}|∇v|, v_{Q'} the mean. Indeed |v(x) − v(y)| ≤ √n s∫_0^1|∇v(x + t(y − x))| dt for x, y ∈ Q'. Integrate over Q' × Q'; for t ≤ 1/2 substitute x ↦ (1 − t)x + ty (Jacobian (1 − t)ⁿ ≥ 2^{−n}, image ⊆ Q' by convexity), and for t ≥ 1/2 substitute y ↦ (1 − t)x + ty (Jacobian tⁿ ≥ 2^{−n}). This gives ∫∫|v(x) − v(y)| dx dy ≤ √n s·2ⁿsⁿ∫_{Q'}|∇v| (≤ the parent's 2^{n+1}√n s^{n+1}∫|∇v|). Since |v(x) − v_{Q'}| ≤ s^{−n}∫_{Q'}|v(x) − v(y)| dy, ∫_{Q'}|v − v_{Q'}| ≤ √n s2ⁿ∫_{Q'}|∇v| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n∫_{Q'}|∇v|.

3. Poincaré inequality for u: ∫_{Q₁}|u − u_{Q₁}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√nV. By 1 and 2 (Q' := closure Q_δ), ∫_{Q_δ}|u_σ − (u_σ)_{Q_δ}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√nV for σ < δ. As σ ↓ 0, u_σ → ū in L¹(ℝⁿ) (L¹ convergence of mollifications), so ∫_{Q_δ}|u − u_{Q_δ}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√nV. As δ ↓ 0, u_{Q_δ} → u_{Q₁} and ∫_{Q_δ}|u − u_{Q_δ}| → ∫_{Q₁}|u − u_{Q₁}| by dominated convergence.

4. Integer median (parent C2). Since u is real-valued and integrable on Q₁, Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ c}) → 1 as c → +∞ and → 0 as c → −∞. Let β be the least integer c with Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ c}) ≥ 1/2. Then Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β}) ≥ 1/2 and, u being integer-valued, Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≥ β}) = 1 − Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β − 1}) > 1/2; so β is a median.
 (a) A median minimizes c ↦ ∫_{Q₁}|u − c|. For c > β, |u − c| − |u − β| ≥ c − β on {u ≤ β} and ≥ −(c − β) on {u > β}, so ∫(|u − c| − |u − β|) ≥ (c − β)(Lⁿ{u ≤ β} − Lⁿ{u > β}) ≥ 0. The case c < β is symmetric, using Lⁿ{u ≥ β} ≥ 1/2. With c = u_{Q₁} and 3: ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ 2^{n+1}√nV (parent C1(i)).
 (b) If β > 0 then u ≥ β on a subset of Q₁ of measure ≥ 1/2, so ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ β/2. If β < 0 then u ≤ β on a set of measure ≥ 1/2, so ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ |β|/2. Hence |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|.

5. Trace estimate (parent C1(ii)). Let G : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ be smooth with |G| ≤ 1, and let w ∈ L¹(Q₁) satisfy the hypothesis of the statement with the constant V. Then |∫_{Q₁} w div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q₁}|w|. (The integral exists: div G is continuous, hence bounded on the compact closure of Q₁.)
 Proof. Let w_σ := (w1_{Q₁}) ∗ φ_σ, σ < δ. Apply the divergence theorem on the box Q_δ to the smooth field w_σG, whose divergence is ∇w_σ·G + w_σ div G (by Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus in each coordinate, ∫_{Q_δ}∂_i(w_σG_i) is the difference of the integrals of w_σG_i over the faces {x_i = 1 − δ} and {x_i = δ}; alternatively Mathlib MeasureTheory.integral_divergence_of_hasFDerivAt_off_countable, transported from Fin n → ℝ to Euclid n). This gives ∫_{Q_δ}w_σ div G = −∫_{Q_δ}∇w_σ·G + ∫_{∂Q_δ}w_σG·ν dH^{n−1}, so |∫_{Q_δ}w_σ div G| ≤ ∫_{Q_δ}|∇w_σ| + ∫_{∂Q_δ}|w_σ|. On the face {x₁ = δ}, |w_σ(δ, x')| ≤ |w_σ(x₁, x')| + ∫_δ^{1−δ}|∂₁w_σ(t, x')| dt for x₁ ∈ (δ, 1 − δ); averaging over x₁ (length s ≥ 1/2) and integrating in x' gives ∫_{face}|w_σ| ≤ 2∫_{Q_δ}|w_σ| + ∫_{Q_δ}|∇w_σ|, and the same holds for all 2n faces (for n = 1 the faces are points and no x'-integration occurs). With 1 applied to w: |∫_{Q_δ}w_σ div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q_δ}|w_σ|. Let σ ↓ 0 (w_σ → w1_{Q₁} in L¹, div G bounded on closure Q₁), then δ ↓ 0 (dominated convergence): |∫_{Q₁}w div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q₁}|w|.

6. Conclusion. Put c := 2^{n+1}√n + (2n + 1) + 4n·2^{n+1}√n > 0 (depending only on m). By 4(a), ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ 2^{n+1}√nV ≤ cV, which is (1); 4(b) is (2). By 0, w := u − β satisfies the hypothesis with V, so by 5 and 4(a), for every smooth G with |G| ≤ 1, |∫_{Q₁}(u − β) div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n·2^{n+1}√nV ≤ cV, which is (3). ∎
proof_key_steps: V ≥ 0, |∫u div g| ≤ V, and u − β satisfies the same hypothesis.
Mollified u_σ satisfies ∫_{Q_δ}|∇u_σ| ≤ V (duality with the fields φ̌_σ ∗ g supported in Q₁).
Smooth Poincaré on cubes of side in [1/2, 1] and the limits σ ↓ 0, δ ↓ 0 give ∫_{Q₁}|u − u_{Q₁}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V.
The least integer β with Lⁿ{u ≤ β} ≥ 1/2 is a median, minimizes c ↦ ∫|u − c| and satisfies |β| ≤ 2∫|u|.
Divergence theorem and the trace inequality on Q_δ give |∫_{Q₁} w div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫|w|; apply it to w = u − β.

subproblem.title: Push-forward by dilations x ↦ λx (scaling of currents, step E0)
subproblem.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ there is an operation dil assigning to every degree k ∈ ℕ, real λ and current X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) (domain univ) a current dil_k(λ, X) ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) such that for every k and every λ > 0: (1) dil_k(λ, X − Y) = dil_k(λ, X) − dil_k(λ, Y) for all X, Y; (2) dil_k(λ⁻¹, dil_k(λ, X)) = X; (3) M(dil_k(λ, X)) = λ^k M(X) (in [0, ∞], factor ENNReal.ofReal (λ^k)); (4) spt dil_k(λ, X) = {λx : x ∈ spt X}; (5) dil_k(λ, X) is integer multiplicity whenever X is (every degree k, including 0); (6) ∂dil_{k+1}(λ, X) = dil_k(λ, ∂X) for X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ P : ℕ, ∃ dil : ∀ k : ℕ, ℝ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k, ∀ (k : ℕ) (lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → (∀ X Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k, dil k lam (X - Y) = dil k lam X - dil k lam Y) ∧ (∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k, dil k lam⁻¹ (dil k lam X) = X) ∧ (∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k, (dil k lam X).mass = ENNReal.ofReal (lam ^ k) * X.mass) ∧ (∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k, (dil k lam X).support = (fun x => lam • x) '' X.support) ∧ (∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k, IsIntegerMultiplicity X → IsIntegerMultiplicity (dil k lam X)) ∧ ∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (k + 1), (dil (k + 1) lam X).boundary = dil k lam X.boundary
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step E0 of the parent proof (the rescaling of Simon Ch. 6, 5.3 from 5.1): δ_{ρ#} (SimonGMT affinePushforward) preserves integer multiplicity (carrier δ_ρ(M), same multiplicity and orientation transported; approximate tangent spaces commute with dilations), scales masses of k-currents by the k-th power of the factor and supports by the factor, and commutes with ∂. Here the factor is called λ and the map is x ↦ λx.

Notation. For λ ≠ 0, δ_λ(x) := λx. For a k-form ω on ℝ^P, (δ_λ^#ω)(x) := ω(λx) ∘ (λ·id), i.e. (δ_λ^#ω)(x)(v_1,…,v_k) = λ^kω(λx)(v_1,…,v_k). |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm and ‖ω‖ := sup_x|ω(x)|.

1. Definition. For λ ≠ 0 the affine map x ↦ 0 + (λ·id)x is a homeomorphism, hence proper. SimonGMT's GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward (λ·id) 0 (Simon 6.2.23) therefore defines, for X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) (domain univ, whose preimage is univ), a current dil_k(λ, X) := δ_{λ#}X with δ_{λ#}X(ω) = X(δ_λ^#ω). For λ = 0 put dil_k(0, X) := X (never used; formally dil is defined by a dependent if on λ ≠ 0, since the properness proof uses λ ≠ 0). Below λ > 0.

subproblem.title: Choice of a good centre for the dual skeleton (step E1; Simon 6.5.1, (1)–(7))
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ with m + 1 < P. There is C ∈ ℝ≥0, depending only on P and m, such that for any two finite Borel measures μ, μ' on ℝ^P (Euclid P) there is a ∈ ℝ^P with |a_i − 1/2| < 1/4 for all i such that, writing L*(a) := {y : there is a finite set s of coordinate indices with |s| ≥ m + 2 and y_i − a_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ s} and d := dist(·, L*(a)) (Metric.infDist), for every r with 0 < r ≤ 1/4: μ({x : d(x) < r}) ≤ C·r^{m+2}·μ(ℝ^P) and μ'({x : d(x) < r}) ≤ C·r^{m+2}·μ'(ℝ^P) (inequalities in [0, ∞], r^{m+2} read via ENNReal.ofReal).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ), m + 1 < P → ∃ C : NNReal, ∀ μ μ' : Measure (Euclid P), IsFiniteMeasure μ → IsFiniteMeasure μ' → ∃ a : Euclid P, (∀ i, |a i - 1 / 2| < 1 / 4) ∧ ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r ≤ 1 / 4 → μ {x | infDist x {w : Euclid P | ∃ s : Finset (Fin P), m + 2 ≤ s.card ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, ∃ z : ℤ, w i - a i = z} < r} ≤ C * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ (m + 2)) * μ univ ∧ μ' {x | infDist x {w : Euclid P | ∃ s : Finset (Fin P), m + 2 ≤ s.card ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, ∃ z : ℤ, w i - a i = z} < r} ≤ C * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ (m + 2)) * μ' univ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step E1 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, displays (1)–(7)) together with Part D's formula for L*(a; ρ), with μ_T and μ_{∂T} replaced by two arbitrary finite Borel measures μ, μ'. The parent states the conclusion as (6), (7) with constant Nβ; here C := Nβ.

Notation. n := m + 1, ℓ := P − n ≥ 1, so n + 1 ≤ P. 𝒥 := the set of J ⊆ {1,…,P} with |J| = n + 1, N := |𝒥| = binom(P, n + 1) (the parent's S_1,…,S_N). For J ∈ 𝒥: S_J := {x : x_i = 0 (i ∉ J)} (dimension n + 1); p_J is the orthogonal projection onto S_J (p_J(x)_i = x_i for i ∈ J, 0 otherwise); S_J^⊥ = {x : x_i = 0 (i ∈ J)} (dimension ℓ − 1); Z_J := ℤ^P ∩ S_J; B^J_r(w) := {v ∈ S_J : |v − w| < r} (Euclidean balls of S_J, i.e. of the PiLp 2 norm, not sup-metric balls). q := (1/2,…,1/2), x_J := p_J(q). L^d is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^d, ω_d := L^d(unit ball), ω_0 := 1. For a ∈ ℝ^P, L*(a) := {y : at least n + 1 = m + 2 coordinates satisfy y_i − a_i ∈ ℤ} and d_a := dist(·, L*(a)).

1. Tubes around the dual skeleton (parent Part D: L*(a; ρ) = ⋃_j⋃_z p_j^{-1}(B_ρ(p_j(a) + z))). For a ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0,
 {x : d_a(x) < r} = ⋃_{J∈𝒥} ⋃_{z∈Z_J} p_J^{-1}(B^J_r(p_J(a) + z)).
 Proof: L*(a) = ⋃_{J,z} A_{J,z} with A_{J,z} := p_J^{-1}(p_J(a) + z) = {y : y_i = a_i + z_i (i ∈ J)}. Indeed, if y ∈ L*(a), choose n + 1 indices J among those with y_i − a_i ∈ ℤ and put z_i := y_i − a_i (i ∈ J), z_i := 0 otherwise; the converse is immediate. For x ∈ ℝ^P, dist(x, A_{J,z}) = |p_J(x) − p_J(a) − z| (Pythagoras; the point x − p_J(x) + p_J(a) + z ∈ A_{J,z} attains it). The distance to a union is the infimum of the distances, so d_a(x) < r iff |p_J(x) − p_J(a) − z| < r for some (J, z).

2. Bad sets (parent: G_j, B_j). Let ν be a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P and β > 0. For g ∈ S_J and r > 0 put O_r(g) := ⋃_{z∈Z_J} p_J^{-1}(B^J_r(g + z)) (open). Let G_J(ν) be the set of g ∈ S_J with |g − x_J| < 1/4 and ν(O_r(g)) ≤ βr^{n+1}ν(ℝ^P) for every r ∈ (0, 1/4], and B_J(ν) := {g ∈ S_J : |g − x_J| < 1/4} ∖ G_J(ν). (The parent intersects with F_j = C ∩ S_j; this changes nothing since B^J_{1/4}(x_J) ⊆ F_J.) If ν(ℝ^P) = 0 then B_J(ν) = ∅. Assume ν(ℝ^P) > 0.
 (2a) B_J(ν) is relatively open in S_J, hence Borel (the parent's "l.s.c. in g"). Let g ∈ B_J(ν) with witness r and g_k → g in S_J. O_r(g_k) = O_r(g) + (g_k − g), and every point of the open set O_r(g) lies in O_r(g_k) for large k. So 1_{O_r(g)} ≤ liminf_k 1_{O_r(g_k)} pointwise and, by Fatou, ν(O_r(g)) ≤ liminf_k ν(O_r(g_k)). Hence ν(O_r(g_k)) > βr^{n+1}ν(ℝ^P) and |g_k − x_J| < 1/4 for large k, i.e. g_k ∈ B_J(ν).
 (2b) L^{n+1}(B_J(ν)) ≤ 5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}/β. For each b ∈ B_J(ν) choose r_b ∈ (0, 1/4] with ν(O_{r_b}(b)) > βr_b^{n+1}ν(ℝ^P). By the 5r-covering lemma (Simon Ch. 1, 3.4; Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement) there is a pairwise disjoint subfamily of the balls B^J_{r_b}(b), countable because S_J is separable, say B^J_{r_l}(b_l), such that every B^J_{r_b}(b) meets some B^J_{r_l}(b_l) with r_b ≤ 2r_l; so B_J(ν) ⊆ ⋃_l B^J_{5r_l}(b_l). The open sets O_{r_l}(b_l) are pairwise disjoint, because the balls B^J_{r_l}(b_l + z) are pairwise disjoint over (l, z): for equal z they are translates of disjoint balls; for z ≠ z' they lie in B^J_{1/2}(x_J + z) and B^J_{1/2}(x_J + z') (|b_l − x_J| < 1/4, r_l ≤ 1/4), which are disjoint since |z − z'| ≥ 1; preimages under p_J of disjoint sets are disjoint. Hence βν(ℝ^P)Σ_l r_l^{n+1} ≤ Σ_l ν(O_{r_l}(b_l)) ≤ ν(ℝ^P), so Σ_l r_l^{n+1} ≤ 1/β and L^{n+1}(B_J(ν)) ≤ Σ_l ω_{n+1}(5r_l)^{n+1} ≤ 5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}/β.

3. Choice of β and a. Put β := 1 + 2N·5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}ω_{ℓ−1}4^{1−ℓ}·4^P/ω_P, so that 2N·5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}β^{−1}·ω_{ℓ−1}4^{1−ℓ} < ω_P4^{−P} (the parent's choice); β depends only on P and m. For J ∈ 𝒥 let Bad_J := {a ∈ B_{1/4}(q) : p_J(a) ∈ B_J(μ) ∪ B_J(μ')} (Borel). If ℓ = 1 then S_J = ℝ^P (J = {1,…,P}, N = 1) and simply Bad_J ⊆ B_J(μ) ∪ B_J(μ'), so L^P(Bad_J) ≤ 2·5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}/β, which is the bound below with ω_0 4^0 = 1. If ℓ ≥ 2, write ℝ^P = S_J ⊕ S_J^⊥; the coordinate splitting x ↦ ((x_i)_{i∈J}, (x_i)_{i∉J}) carries Lebesgue measure on Euclid P to the product of the Lebesgue measures (a measure-preserving coordinate permutation; e.g. Mathlib EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp and measurePreserving_piEquivPiSubtypeProd). Fubini gives
 L^P(Bad_J) = ∫_{B_J(μ)∪B_J(μ')} L^{ℓ−1}({w ∈ S_J^⊥ : g + w ∈ B_{1/4}(q)}) dL^{n+1}(g) ≤ (2·5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}/β)·ω_{ℓ−1}4^{1−ℓ},
because each fibre lies in a ball of radius 1/4 of the (ℓ − 1)-dimensional space S_J^⊥. Summing over the N sets J, L^P(⋃_J Bad_J) ≤ 2N·5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}ω_{ℓ−1}4^{1−ℓ}/β < ω_P4^{−P} = L^P(B_{1/4}(q)). Choose a ∈ B_{1/4}(q) ∖ ⋃_J Bad_J. Then |a_i − 1/2| ≤ |a − q| < 1/4 for every i. For every J, |p_J(a) − x_J| ≤ |a − q| < 1/4 and p_J(a) ∉ B_J(μ) ∪ B_J(μ'), so p_J(a) ∈ G_J(μ) if μ(ℝ^P) > 0 and p_J(a) ∈ G_J(μ') if μ'(ℝ^P) > 0 (the parent's p_j(a) ∈ G_j ∩ G'_j).

4. Conclusion (parent (6), (7)). Let r ∈ (0, 1/4]. By 1, {x : d_a(x) < r} = ⋃_J O_r(p_J(a)), hence μ({d_a < r}) ≤ Σ_J μ(O_r(p_J(a))) ≤ Nβr^{n+1}μ(ℝ^P); if μ(ℝ^P) = 0 both sides vanish. The same holds for μ'. Thus C := Nβ ∈ ℝ≥0, depending only on P and m, satisfies μ({x : d_a(x) < r}) ≤ C·r^{m+2}·μ(univ) and μ'({x : d_a(x) < r}) ≤ C·r^{m+2}·μ'(univ) for all r ∈ (0, 1/4] (in [0, ∞], r^{m+2} = r^{n+1} via ENNReal.ofReal), and a satisfies |a_i − 1/2| < 1/4 for all i. ∎
proof_key_steps: {d_a < r} is the union over (n+1)-subsets J and z ∈ ℤ^P ∩ S_J of the cylinders p_J^{-1}(B_r(p_J(a) + z)) (Part D's formula for L*(a; r)).

For each J and each measure, the set of bad projections g (some r ≤ 1/4 with ν(O_r(g)) > βr^{n+1}ν(ℝ^P)) is relatively open (Fatou) and has L^{n+1}-measure ≤ 5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}/β by the 5r-covering lemma and disjointness of the periodic cylinders.
Fubini over S_J × S_J^⊥ bounds the measure of centres a ∈ B_{1/4}(q) with a bad projection by 2·5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}ω_{ℓ−1}4^{1−ℓ}/β; for the parent's β the union over J misses a point a.
For this a, μ({d_a < r}) ≤ Σ_J μ(O_r(p_J(a))) ≤ Nβr^{n+1}μ(ℝ^P), likewise for μ'; C := Nβ.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the closing step of B3 in the parent proof — from "Injective area formula: Φ_F(ω) = Σ_{il}∫_{N_{il}} g_{il}⟨ω, η_{il}⟩dHᵏ, Σ_{il}∫|g_{il}| = I'_F" to "(N', |m|, sign(m)η) is an IMRep representing Φ_F" — stated for an arbitrary mass-summable sequence of integer multiplicity currents instead of the pieces (N_{il}, |g_{il}|, sign(g_{il})η_{il}); together with the elementary fact, used in the parent's E4 ("mass, hence weak, limits"), that a mass-summable series of currents defines a current with the obvious mass and support bounds. The combination argument is the parent's: finite total multiplicity, almost every point in finitely many pieces, a common approximate tangent plane by (IMC)(a), orientations equal up to sign by (L3), an integer multiplicity m, and the IMRep (N', |m|, sign(m)η).

Notation. All currents are in 𝒟_{n'}(ℝ^P) with domain univ, n' := k + 1. ‖ω‖ := sup_x|ω(x)| (Euclidean coefficient norm). (VO), (MR), (IMC) are the three displayed hypotheses of the statement.

1. Evaluation bound. For every current X and test form ω, |X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖ (in [0, ∞]). Indeed, for ε > 0 the forms ±ω/(‖ω‖ + ε) are admissible for M(X) (support in univ, |·| ≤ 1), so ±X(ω) ≤ (‖ω‖ + ε)M(X); let ε ↓ 0.

2. Definition of S. Let A := Σ_i M(W_i) < ∞. For each ω, Σ_i|W_i(ω)| ≤ A‖ω‖ < ∞, so S(ω) := Σ_iW_i(ω) converges absolutely; in particular HasSum (i ↦ W_i(ω)) (S(ω)). S is linear. Continuity: if ω_j → 0 in the test-form topology (supports in one compact set, all iterated derivatives → 0 uniformly), then sup_x of the operator norm of ω_j(x) tends to 0; the Euclidean coefficient norm is bounded by a constant C(P, n') times the operator norm (each coefficient ω(x)(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_{n'}}) is bounded by the operator norm), so ‖ω_j‖ → 0 and |S(ω_j)| ≤ A‖ω_j‖ → 0. So S ∈ 𝒟_{n'}(ℝ^P).

3. Mass. For admissible ω, S(ω) = Σ_iW_i(ω) ≤ Σ_iM(W_i), so M(S) ≤ Σ_iM(W_i).

4. Support. Let E := closure ⋃_i spt W_i and x ∉ E. Choose r > 0 with closedBall(x, r) ∩ E = ∅. The open ball B := ball(x, r) has compact closure. Every test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ B satisfies tsupport ω ∩ spt W_i = ∅ for all i, hence W_i(ω) = 0 by (VO) and S(ω) = 0. So x lies in the zero region of S, i.e. spt S ⊆ E.

5. Integer multiplicity (the parent's B3 closing step). Assume every W_i is integer multiplicity, with IMRep R_i = (M_i, θ_i, ξ_i). By (MR) (U = W = univ, open), ∫_{M_i}θ_i dH^{n'} = R_i.measure(ℝ^P) = M(W_i). Modifying ξ_i on an H^{n'}⌞M_i-null set, we may take ξ_i Borel (this changes neither the action nor the a.e. orientation property).
 (5a) N := ⋃_iM_i is Borel and countably n'-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion), and H^{n'}(N) ≤ Σ_iH^{n'}(M_i) ≤ Σ_i∫_{M_i}θ_i dH^{n'} = A < ∞ because θ_i ≥ 1 on M_i.
 (5b) Θ := Σ_iθ_i1_{M_i} : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] has ∫Θ dH^{n'} = A, so Θ < ∞ off an H^{n'}-null set; at such points only finitely many i have x ∈ M_i (θ_i ≥ 1 there).
 (5c) Tangent planes. For each i apply (IMC)(a) with U = univ, M = M_i ⊆ M' = N (both Borel, H^{n'}(N ∩ K) ≤ A < ∞): for H^{n'}-a.e. x ∈ M_i and every subspace Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n' M_i x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n' N x Q. By the orientation field of R_i, for H^{n'}-a.e. x ∈ M_i there is Q_i(x) with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n' M_i x Q_i(x) and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_i(x)) (Q_i(x)). Removing a countable union of null sets, for H^{n'}-a.e. x ∈ N each i with x ∈ M_i gives an approximate tangent space Q_i(x) of N at x; by uniqueness (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) these coincide; call the common value Q(x).
 (5d) Signs. Let ι(x) := min{i : x ∈ M_i} for x ∈ N (Borel) and η(x) := ξ_{ι(x)}(x) (Borel). Two unit orientations of the same n'-dimensional subspace differ by a sign (the sign rule (L3) of the parent, proved here; cf. Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det): if ξ = ±(α ↦ α(τ)) and ξ' = ±(α ↦ α(τ')) with orthonormal bases τ, τ' of Q, then τ' = Oτ for an orthogonal O and α(τ') = det(O)α(τ) = ±α(τ) for every alternating α. Put s_i(x) := 1 if ‖ξ_i(x) − η(x)‖ ≤ ‖ξ_i(x) + η(x)‖ and s_i(x) := −1 otherwise (Borel). A unit orientation is nonzero (it takes the value ±1 on a covector dual to its orthonormal frame). So for H^{n'}-a.e. x ∈ N and every i with x ∈ M_i, ξ_i(x) = s_i(x)η(x).
 (5e) Multiplicity. m(x) := Σ_is_i(x)θ_i(x)1_{M_i}(x) (m := 0 where Θ(x) = ∞) is Borel, as a pointwise limit of finite sums of Borel integer-valued functions. H^{n'}-a.e. on N it is a finite sum of integers, and |m| ≤ Θ, so m is integer-valued a.e. with ∫|m| dH^{n'} ≤ A.
 (5f) Action. For a test form ω, |ξ_i(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ ‖ω‖ for a.e. x ∈ M_i ((IMC)(d)), so Σ_i∫θ_i1_{M_i}|ξ_i(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖A. Dominated convergence for series gives
 S(ω) = Σ_i∫_{M_i}θ_iξ_i(x)(ω(x)) dH^{n'} = ∫_NΣ_iθ_i1_{M_i}s_iη(x)(ω(x)) dH^{n'} = ∫_N m(x)η(x)(ω(x)) dH^{n'}.
 (5g) The IMRep. Let Z ⊆ N be a Borel H^{n'}-null set outside of which (5b)–(5e) hold. Put N' := {x ∈ N ∖ Z : m(x) ≠ 0} (Borel), mult := N'.indicator (Int.natAbs ∘ m) (Borel, ℕ-valued, positive on N'), and orient := sign(m)η. The IMRep fields hold: N' ⊆ univ; N' ⊆ N is countably n'-rectifiable (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono); ∫_{N'∩K}|m| ≤ A < ∞; orient is Borel, hence a.e. strongly measurable; and for H^{n'}-a.e. x ∈ N', (IMC)(a) with M = N' ⊆ M' = N shows that Q(x), an approximate tangent space of N at x, is also one of N' at x, and sign(m(x))η(x) is a unit orientation of Q(x) (IsUnitOrientationOf allows either sign). Its action is ∫_{N'}|m|sign(m)η(ω) dH^{n'} = ∫_N mη(ω) dH^{n'} = S(ω) (m = 0 on N ∖ (N' ∪ Z)). Hence S is integer multiplicity.

6. The current S of 2 satisfies the four conclusions by 2, 3, 4 and 5. ∎
proof_key_steps: |X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖, so S(ω) := Σ_i W_i(ω) converges absolutely and defines a sequentially continuous linear functional.
M(S) ≤ Σ M(W_i) on admissible forms; spt S ⊆ closure ⋃ spt W_i by (VO).
For integer multiplicity W_i with IMReps (M_i, θ_i, ξ_i): N := ⋃M_i has finite Hausdorff measure by (MR), and a.e. point lies in finitely many M_i.
By (IMC)(a) and uniqueness all M_i containing x share the approximate tangent space of N at x; the orientations differ from a Borel reference orientation η by signs ((L3)).
The integer multiplicity m := Σ s_iθ_i1_{M_i} and dominated convergence give S(ω) = ∫_N mη(ω)dH, and (N', |m|, sign(m)η) is an IMRep of S (closing step of B3).

subproblem.title: Retraction onto the n-skeleton away from the dual skeleton (Lemma D; Simon 6.5.4)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ with m + 1 < P and put n := m + 1. There is a constant c > 0, depending only on P and m, such that for every a ∈ ℝ^P (Euclid P) with |a_i − 1/2| < 1/4 for all i the following holds. Let L*(a) := {y ∈ ℝ^P : there is a finite set s of coordinate indices with |s| ≥ m + 2 and y_i − a_i ∈ ℤ for all i ∈ s} (the dual skeleton) and d(x) := dist(x, L*(a)) (Metric.infDist). Then there is a map ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P such that (i) for every x with d(x) > 0, ψ(x) lies in the n-skeleton of the unit cubical grid, i.e. there is a set s of coordinate indices with P ≤ n + |s| and ψ(x)_i ∈ ℤ for all i ∈ s, and |ψ(x) − x| ≤ √P; (ii) for every r with 0 < r ≤ 1/4 and all x, y with d(x) ≥ r and d(y) ≥ r, |ψ(x) − ψ(y)| ≤ (c/r)|x − y|.

Source: Part D (Lemma D and its proof) of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 5.4 and its proof, displays (1)–(8). Two adjustments, both already present in the parent: (a) the documented erratum — Simon's "|y − a| ≥ 3/4" (a ∈ B_{1/4}(q), y ∈ ∂C) is false (take a = q and y the centre of a facet, |y − a| = 1/2) and is replaced by |y − a| > 1/4, which changes only constants; (b) the parent's hypothesis a ∈ B_{1/4}(q) is used only through a_i ∈ (1/4, 3/4) for every i, so the statement assumes exactly that (it is implied by a ∈ B_{1/4}(q) since |a_i − 1/2| ≤ |a − q|). Lemma D's constant c₂ = 2c₁ + 8√P + 1 is the constant c below.

Notation. n := m + 1 and ℓ := P − n ≥ 1. For J ⊆ {1,…,P} with |J| = j and b ∈ ℤ^P, the closed j-face F = F(b, J) := {x : b_i ≤ x_i ≤ b_i + 1 (i ∈ J), x_i = b_i (i ∉ J)}; J are its free coordinates, aff F := {x : x_i = b_i (i ∉ J)}, F̆ is its relative interior and ∂F := F ∖ F̆ (the union of its (j − 1)-faces). L_j := union of all closed j-faces (the j-skeleton). A point x lies in L_j iff at least P − j of its coordinates are integers: a point of F(b, J) has the P − j integer coordinates x_i = b_i (i ∉ J); conversely if x_i ∈ ℤ for i in a set of P − j indices, let J be the complementary j indices, b_i := ⌊x_i⌋ (i ∈ J), b_i := x_i (i ∉ J). So x ∈ L_n is exactly the statement's condition "∃ s, P ≤ n + |s|, x_i ∈ ℤ (i ∈ s)". C := [0,1]^P. By hypothesis a_i ∈ (1/4, 3/4) for all i. L*(a) is the set of y with at least n + 1 coordinates in a_i + ℤ (this is the parent's a + L_{ℓ−1}); it is a locally finite union of affine planes {y : y_i = a_i + z_i (i ∈ J')} (|J'| = n + 1, z ∈ ℤ^{J'}), hence closed, and it contains a. d(x) := dist(x, L*(a)) is 1-Lipschitz, d(x) ≤ |x − a|, and d(x) > 0 iff x ∉ L*(a). For a map f and a point x of its domain, D̄f(x) := limsup_{y→x} |f(y) − f(x)|/|y − x| (y in the domain), the pointwise upper Lipschitz constant.

1. Centres of faces. For a face F = F(b, J) with |J| = j ≥ n + 1 let a_F be the orthogonal projection of a onto aff F: (a_F)_i := b_i + a_i (i ∈ J), (a_F)_i := b_i (i ∉ J). Since a_i ∈ (1/4, 3/4), a_F ∈ F̆, and every point of ∂F (some free coordinate equal to b_i or b_i + 1) has distance > 1/4 from a_F. F − a_F contains the ball of radius 1/4 of the plane V_J := span{e_i : i ∈ J} and is contained in the ball of radius √j. A face shared by two cubes gets the same centre (a_F is defined from F alone), and translating F by z ∈ ℤ^P translates a_F by z.

2. The dual skeleton meets a face in a cone (parent (1); Simon (1)–(2)). Let F = F(b, J), |J| = j ≥ n + 1. Then L*(a) ∩ F = U_F ∩ F, where U_F := ⋃{Π_{J'} : J' ⊆ J, |J'| = n + 1} and Π_{J'} := {x ∈ aff F : x_i = (a_F)_i (i ∈ J')}. Proof: if x ∈ F ∩ L*(a), take s with |s| ≥ n + 1 and x_i − a_i ∈ ℤ (i ∈ s). For i ∉ J, x_i = b_i ∈ ℤ while a_i ∉ ℤ, so s ⊆ J. For i ∈ s, x_i − b_i ∈ [0, 1] and x_i − b_i ≡ a_i (mod 1) with a_i ∈ (1/4, 3/4), so x_i = b_i + a_i = (a_F)_i; any J' ⊆ s with |J'| = n + 1 gives x ∈ Π_{J'}. Conversely, if x ∈ F ∩ Π_{J'} then x_i − a_i = b_i ∈ ℤ for the n + 1 indices i ∈ J', so x ∈ L*(a). Each Π_{J'} is an affine subspace of aff F through a_F. Hence U_F is invariant under every homothety of aff F centred at a_F with nonzero ratio (L*(a) ∩ F is a cone with vertex a_F), and a_F ∈ L*(a).

3. Radial retractions. For F as in 2 let N_F be the gauge of the convex body F − a_F in V_J, N_F(v) = max_{i∈J} max(v_i/(1 − a_i), −v_i/a_i), and ψ_F(x) := a_F + (x − a_F)/N_F(x − a_F) for x ∈ F ∖ {a_F}: the point of ∂F on the ray from a_F through x (the parent's radial retraction). ψ_F = id on ∂F. By 1, N_F is 4-Lipschitz (each functional has norm < 4 as a_i, 1 − a_i > 1/4) and N_F(v) ≥ max_i|v_i| ≥ |v|/√j. If x ∈ F ∖ L*(a) then x ∉ U_F, hence ψ_F(x) = a_F + λ(x − a_F) (λ > 0) ∉ U_F by homothety invariance, hence ψ_F(x) ∈ ∂F ∖ L*(a) by 2. If x lies in two j-faces F ≠ F', it lies in their intersection, a face of dimension < j, so x ∈ ∂F ∩ ∂F' and ψ_F(x) = x = ψ_{F'}(x). Hence ψ^{(j)} := ⋃_{|J|=j}ψ_F is a well-defined map L_j ∖ L*(a) → L_{j−1} ∖ L*(a) (as a function one may evaluate ψ^{(j)}(x) := ψ_F(x) for a canonically chosen j-face F containing x, e.g. the one with the lexicographically least (J, b); by the above the value does not depend on the choice), continuous because the j-faces form a locally finite closed cover of L_j and each ψ_F is continuous on F ∖ {a_F}. Radial estimate: for x, y ∈ F ∖ {a_F}, v := x − a_F, w := y − a_F,
 |ψ_F(x) − ψ_F(y)| = |v/N_F(v) − w/N_F(w)| ≤ |v − w|/N_F(v) + |w||N_F(w) − N_F(v)|/(N_F(v)N_F(w)) ≤ (1 + 4√j)√j|v − w|/|v|,
so D̄(ψ_F|F)(x) ≤ (1 + 4√j)√j/|x − a_F|.

4. Definition of ψ (parent: ψ₀ := ψ^{(n+1)} ∘ ⋯ ∘ ψ^{(P)} on C ∖ L*(a), extended periodically). On ℝ^P ∖ L*(a) put ψ := ψ^{(n+1)} ∘ ψ^{(n+2)} ∘ ⋯ ∘ ψ^{(P)} (L_P = ℝ^P); by 3 it is well defined and continuous with values in L_n ∖ L*(a). On L*(a) put ψ := id (never used). This proves the first half of (i) for every x with d(x) > 0. Same cube: if x ∈ z + C (z ∈ ℤ^P) and x ∉ L*(a), then ψ^{(P)}(x) = ψ_{z+C}(x) ∈ z + C; inductively, if y ∈ (z + C) ∩ L_j ∖ L*(a), then y lies in a j-face G ⊆ z + C (its integer coordinates are z_i or z_i + 1; fix P − j of them) and ψ^{(j)}(y) = ψ_G(y) ∈ ∂G ⊆ z + C (any j-face containing y gives the same value, by 3). Hence ψ(x) ∈ z + C and |ψ(x) − x| ≤ diam(z + C) = √P, the second half of (i). Also ψ(z + x) = z + ψ(x) (z ∈ ℤ^P), since L*(a) + z = L*(a) and faces, centres and retractions translate accordingly.

5. Pointwise bound (parent: D̄ψ ≤ c₁/d; Simon (3)): D̄ψ(x) ≤ c₁(P, n)/d(x) for every x with d(x) > 0. By induction on ℓ = P − n ≥ 1, simultaneously for all P, n with that codimension and all a with a_i ∈ (1/4, 3/4). The closed unit cubes not containing x form a closed set missing x, so points y near x lie in the finitely many closed cubes containing x, and D̄ψ(x) ≤ max over those cubes of D̄(ψ|cube)(x); by periodicity it suffices to bound D̄(ψ|C)(x) for x ∈ C.
 (5a) ℓ = 1 (P = n + 1). By 2 with F = C (only J' = J), L*(a) ∩ C = {a}, and ψ = ψ_C on C. By 3, D̄(ψ|C)(x) ≤ (1 + 4√P)√P/|x − a| ≤ (1 + 4√P)√P/d(x) (a ∈ L*(a)). So c₁(n + 1, n) := (1 + 4√(n+1))√(n+1).
 (5b) ℓ ≥ 2. On C ∖ L*(a), ψ = ψ̃ ∘ ψ_C with ψ_C = ψ^{(P)} and ψ̃ := ψ^{(n+1)} ∘ ⋯ ∘ ψ^{(P−1)} on ∂C ∖ L*(a). Let y₀ := ψ_C(x) ∈ ∂C and let F = F(b, J) be a (P − 1)-face of C containing y₀, J = {1,…,P} ∖ {i₀}, b_{i₀} ∈ {0, 1}, b_i = 0 (i ∈ J). Identify aff F with ℝ^{P−1} by deleting the coordinate i₀. Then: the grid faces lying in aff F are the grid faces of ℝ^{P−1}; the centre of a face G ⊆ aff F is the centre of G for a' := (a_i)_{i≠i₀} (coordinates in (1/4, 3/4)); L := L*(a) ∩ aff F is the dual skeleton of ℝ^{P−1} for a' and the same n (b_{i₀} ∈ ℤ is never in a_{i₀} + ℤ); and ψ̃ on aff F ∖ L is the map of this construction for (P − 1, n, a'), of codimension ℓ − 1 ≥ 1 (a point of aff F ∩ L_j lies in a j-face G ⊆ aff F, and by 3 ψ^{(j)} may be computed with G). By the induction hypothesis, D̄(ψ̃|F)(y₀) ≤ c₁(P − 1, n)/dist(y₀, L).
 Distance estimate (Simon (4)–(6), corrected). L is the union over J' ⊆ J, |J'| = n + 1, and integers z_i (i ∈ J') of the planes {u ∈ aff F : u_i = a_i + z_i (i ∈ J')}. Let L₀ be the union of those with all z_i = 0 (the planes through a_F of 2) and L₁ the union of the others. If some z_i ≠ 0, then a_i + z_i has distance > 1/4 from [0, 1], so dist(y₀, L₁) ≥ 1/4 for y₀ ∈ F. Let K₀ := ⋃_{J'}{u ∈ ℝ^P : u_i = a_i (i ∈ J')} (J' ⊆ J, |J'| = n + 1) = p_F^{-1}(L₀), p_F the orthogonal projection onto aff F. Then K₀ ⊆ L*(a); K₀ is a union of affine subspaces through a, hence invariant under homotheties centred at a; and dist(u, K₀) = dist(u, L₀) for u ∈ aff F (the coordinate i₀ is unconstrained in each plane of K₀). Since x ∈ C, y₀ = a + λ(x − a) with λ := |y₀ − a|/|x − a| = 1/N_C(x − a) ≥ 1. Therefore dist(y₀, L₀) = dist(y₀, K₀) = λ dist(x, K₀) ≥ λ d(x). As d(x) ≤ |x − a|, λd(x) ≤ |y₀ − a| ≤ √P, so dist(y₀, L) ≥ min(λd(x), 1/4) ≥ λd(x)/(4√P).
 Chain rule (Simon (7)–(8)). Choose δ > 0 such that every (P − 1)-face of C meeting B_δ(y₀) contains y₀ (the finitely many faces not containing y₀ have positive distance from it), and, given ε > 0, such that the induction bound holds up to ε on B_δ(y₀) for each of the finitely many faces containing y₀. By continuity of ψ_C, ψ_C(y) ∈ B_δ(y₀) for y ∈ C close to x; then, with F_y a (P − 1)-face containing ψ_C(y) and y₀,
 |ψ(y) − ψ(x)| ≤ (D̄(ψ̃|F_y)(y₀) + ε)|ψ_C(y) − y₀| ≤ (max_F D̄(ψ̃|F)(y₀) + ε)(D̄(ψ_C|C)(x) + ε)|y − x|.
 Using 3 for ψ_C and the corrected bound |y₀ − a| > 1/4 (a coordinate of y₀ is 0 or 1 and a_i ∈ (1/4, 3/4)):
 D̄(ψ|C)(x) ≤ (4√P c₁(P − 1, n)/(λd(x)))·((1 + 4√P)√P/|x − a|) = 4P(1 + 4√P)c₁(P − 1, n)/(|y₀ − a| d(x)) ≤ 16P(1 + 4√P)c₁(P − 1, n)/d(x).
 So c₁(P, n) := 16P(1 + 4√P)c₁(P − 1, n) works; it depends only on P and n. For x on ∂C the same computation applies with y₀ = x (ψ_C = id on ∂C, λ = 1). Taking the maximum over the closed cubes containing x (each handled by translation, with centre a + z ∈ L*(a)) gives D̄ψ(x) ≤ c₁/d(x), c₁ := c₁(P, n).
 Remark (an equivalent organization of 5 inside ℝ^P, convenient for formalization; same estimates, only the ambient d is used). For n + 1 ≤ j ≤ P let Ψ_j := ψ^{(n+1)} ∘ ⋯ ∘ ψ^{(j)} on L_j ∖ L*(a) and prove by induction on j that D̄(Ψ_j|L_j)(y) ≤ C_j/d(y) for y ∈ L_j with d(y) > 0 (then ψ = Ψ_P and c₁ := C_P). Points of L_j near y lie in j-faces containing y, so it suffices to treat one j-face G = F(b, J) ∋ y. For j = n + 1, L*(a) ∩ G = {a_G} by 2, and 3 gives D̄(ψ_G|G)(y) ≤ (1 + 4√j)√j/|y − a_G| ≤ (1 + 4√j)√j/d(y). For j > n + 1 let y₀ := ψ_G(y) = a_G + λ(y − a_G), λ := 1/N_G(y − a_G) ≥ 1. Let K_G := ⋃{{u ∈ ℝ^P : u_i = b_i + a_i (i ∈ J')} : J' ⊆ J, |J'| = n + 1}; each such plane lies in L*(a) and passes through a_G, so K_G is invariant under homotheties centred at a_G and dist(y₀, K_G) = λdist(y, K_G) ≥ λd(y). Every other plane {u : u_i = a_i + z_i (i ∈ J')} of L*(a) has distance > 1/4 from G: if some i ∈ J' is fixed for G then |a_i + z_i − b_i| > 1/4; if J' ⊆ J and z_i ≠ b_i for some i ∈ J', then dist(a_i + z_i, [b_i, b_i + 1]) > 1/4. Hence d(y₀) ≥ min(λd(y), 1/4) ≥ λd(y)/(4√P), because λd(y) ≤ λ|y − a_G| = |y₀ − a_G| ≤ √j ≤ √P. With the induction hypothesis at y₀ ∈ L_{j−1}, the radial bound D̄(ψ_G|G)(y) ≤ (1 + 4√j)√j/|y − a_G| = (1 + 4√j)√jλ/|y₀ − a_G| < 4(1 + 4√j)√jλ (|y₀ − a_G| > 1/4 by 1) and the chain rule as above, D̄(Ψ_j|G)(y) ≤ (4√PC_{j−1}/(λd(y)))·4(1 + 4√j)√jλ = 16√P(1 + 4√j)√jC_{j−1}/d(y); so C_j := 16√P(1 + 4√j)√jC_{j−1} works (for y ∈ ∂G, y₀ = y and λ = 1).

6. Lipschitz bound on {d ≥ r} (end of the parent's Lemma D). Let 0 < r ≤ 1/4 and d(x), d(y) ≥ r.
 (6a) |x − y| < r/2. Every w ∈ [x, y] has d(w) ≥ d(x) − |w − x| > r/2, so D̄ψ(w) < 2c₁/r by 5. The function f(t) := ψ(x + t(y − x)) is continuous on [0, 1] with limsup_{s→t}|f(s) − f(t)|/|s − t| ≤ (2c₁/r)|y − x| for every t. Then |f(1) − f(0)| ≤ (2c₁/r)|y − x|: for ε > 0 let t* := sup{t ∈ [0, 1] : |f(s) − f(0)| ≤ ((2c₁/r)|y − x| + ε)s for all s ≤ t}; by continuity the inequality holds at t*, and if t* < 1 the bound at t* extends it to [t*, t* + δ] for some δ > 0, a contradiction; let ε ↓ 0.
 (6b) |x − y| ≥ r/2. By (i), |ψ(x) − ψ(y)| ≤ |ψ(x) − x| + |x − y| + |y − ψ(y)| ≤ 2√P + |x − y| ≤ (4√P/r)|x − y| + (1/(4r))|x − y|, using r ≤ 1/4.
 Hence (ii) holds with c := 2c₁ + 8√P + 1 > 0 (the parent's c₂), which depends only on P and m. ∎
proof_key_steps: Faces F(b, J), centres a_F (projection of a onto aff F, free coordinates b_i + a_i), distance > 1/4 from a_F to ∂F.
L*(a) ∩ F is the union of the affine planes of aff F through a_F (prescribed coordinates must be free and equal b_i + a_i), hence a cone with vertex a_F.
Radial retractions ψ_F map F ∖ L*(a) into ∂F ∖ L*(a), agree on common faces, and satisfy D̄ψ_F(x) ≤ (1 + 4√j)√j/|x − a_F|.
ψ := ψ^{(n+1)} ∘ ⋯ ∘ ψ^{(P)} maps {d > 0} into L_n, keeps each point in its closed unit cube (|ψ(x) − x| ≤ √P) and is ℤ^P-periodic.

Induction on ℓ = P − n: D̄ψ ≤ c₁/d, via the (P − 1)-face induction hypothesis, the split L = L₀ ∪ L₁ (translated planes at distance ≥ 1/4), homogeneity of K₀ = p_F^{-1}(L₀) ⊆ L*(a) about a, and the corrected bound |ψ_C(x) − a| > 1/4 (Simon prints 3/4).
Segment argument for |x − y| < r/2 and the bound 2√P + |x − y| otherwise give the Lipschitz constant (2c₁ + 8√P + 1)/r on {d ≥ r}.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps E6–E7 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, displays (26)–(37)) and the finite-family part of E0, in the unit grid (the parent rescales afterwards, see the parent's E0/E8). The cube estimates C1–C2 are the sibling dimred_mbl_dt_cube_bv_median (CB). The parent bounds its V_F by μ_{∂Q₀}(F̆), using the measure of ∂Q₀; here the corresponding number is Var_F := M_{N_F}(∂Q₀) for explicit pairwise disjoint open neighbourhoods N_F (the parent's "neighbourhood N of spt g with N ∩ L_n ⊆ F̆"), which needs no measure representation of ∂Q₀. Below, V_F denotes the coordinate n-plane of F and Var_F that number.

Notation. n := m + 1. (VO), (MR), (IMC) are the three displayed hypotheses. Currents are on univ in ℝ^P; |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm, ‖ω‖ := sup|ω(x)|, and |X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖. Support facts: spt(A − B) ⊆ spt A ∪ spt B, spt ∂A ⊆ spt A, spt 0 = ∅, and a current vanishing on all test forms supported off a closed set E has support in E. Hⁿ := μHE[n], Lⁿ is Lebesgue measure, Q₁ := (0,1)ⁿ.

1. Trivial case n > P (parent E0). Every n-covector on ℝ^P vanishes (n vectors in ℝ^P are linearly dependent), so every n-current is 0. Take c := 1 and 𝒬₀ := {0}; for Q₀ = 0 take Pc := 0 (0 and ∂0 = 0 are integer multiplicity, all masses are 0, spt 0 = ∅). From now on n ≤ P; let c_B be CB's constant and c := max(2, 1 + c_B).

2. Faces. For I = {i_1 < ⋯ < i_n} ⊆ {1,…,P} and b ∈ ℤ^P, F = F(b, I) := {x : b_i ≤ x_i ≤ b_i + 1 (i ∈ I), x_i = b_i (i ∉ I)} is an n-face (of the unit grid). Further:
 - F̆ := {b_i < x_i < b_i + 1 (i ∈ I), x_i = b_i (i ∉ I)}, Π_F := {x : x_i = b_i (i ∉ I)}, V_F := span{e_i : i ∈ I};
 - e_F is the n-vector α ↦ α(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_n}) (a unit orientation of V_F);
 - φ_F(y) := b + Σ_jy_je_{i_j} is an affine isometric embedding ℝⁿ → ℝ^P with φ_F(Q₁) = F̆ and φ_F([0,1]ⁿ) = F;
 - p̃_F(x) := (x_{i_j} − b_{i_j})_j and p_F := φ_F ∘ p̃_F (orthogonal projection onto Π_F);
 - δ_F(y) := dist(y, F ∖ F̆) = min_jmin(y_{i_j} − b_{i_j}, b_{i_j} + 1 − y_{i_j}) for y ∈ F̆.
 Hⁿ⌞Π_F is the image of Lⁿ under φ_F (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so Hⁿ(F̆) = Hⁿ(F) = 1 and Hⁿ(F ∖ F̆) = 0; diam F = √n ≤ √P. The union of the n-faces is L_n = {x : at least P − n integer coordinates}. L_{n−1} (at least P − n + 1 integer coordinates) is the union of the (n−1)-faces and has Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0 (each (n−1)-face is covered by k^{n−1} sets of diameter √n/k, so its Hⁿ-measure is ≤ Ck^{n−1}k^{−n} → 0). L_n ∖ L_{n−1} is the disjoint union of the F̆ (for x with exactly P − n integer coordinates, I := the others, b_i := ⌊x_i⌋ (i ∈ I), b_i := x_i (i ∉ I)). Face currents: [[F]](ω) := ∫_F⟨ω, e_F⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{[0,1]ⁿ}ω(φ_Fy)(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_n}) dy is a current (|[[F]](ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖) with spt [[F]] ⊆ F.
 Lemma 2.1: if y ∈ F̆ and G ≠ F is an n-face, then dist(y, G) ≥ δ_F(y). (The same statement and proof hold for distinct j-faces of any common dimension j ≥ 1; it is used for j = n − 1 ≥ 1 in 8, the case n − 1 = 0 being treated there directly.) Proof: let z ∈ G. Then |y − z| ≥ |y − p_F(z)|. If p_F(z) ∉ F̆, some free coordinate of p_F(z) lies outside (b_i, b_i + 1), so |y − p_F(z)| ≥ δ_F(y). Otherwise the coordinates z_i (i ∈ I) are non-integers, hence free coordinates of G; as G has exactly n free coordinates, they are I, and z_i ∈ (b_i, b_i + 1) forces G = F(b', I) with b'_i = b_i (i ∈ I). G ≠ F gives b'_k ≠ b_k for some k ∉ I, and |y − z| ≥ |b_k − b'_k| ≥ 1 ≥ δ_F(y).
 Neighbourhoods: N_F := {x : p_F(x) ∈ F̆, |x − p_F(x)| < δ_F(p_F(x))/2} is open.
 (i) N_F ∩ L_n ⊆ F̆: if x ∈ N_F ∩ G for an n-face G ≠ F, then y := p_F(x) ∈ F̆ satisfies |x − y| < δ_F(y)/2 ≤ dist(y, G)/2 ≤ |x − y|/2, impossible. So x ∈ F ⊆ Π_F and p_F(x) = x ∈ F̆.
 (ii) N_F ∩ N_{F'} = ∅ for F ≠ F': with y := p_F(x), y' := p_{F'}(x), Lemma 2.1 gives |y − y'| ≥ max(δ_F(y), δ_{F'}(y')), while |y − y'| < (δ_F(y) + δ_{F'}(y'))/2.
 Finite family (parent E0). Given K (compact) and Λ, let 𝔉_K be the set of n-faces contained in cthickening(√P, K), a finite set (a bounded set contains finitely many unit faces), and 𝒬₀ := {Σ_{F∈𝔉_K}β_F[[F]] : β : 𝔉_K → ℤ, Σ_F|β_F| ≤ 2Λ}, where Σβ_F[[F]] is the current ω ↦ Σβ_F[[F]](ω). 𝒬₀ is finite (the image of a finite set of integer coefficient vectors) and does not depend on Q₀.

3. Decomposition on open faces (parent E6; Simon (33)). Let Q₀ be as in the statement, R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep and μ := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M. By (MR), μ(W) = M_W(Q₀) for open W, so μ(ℝ^P) = M(Q₀). By (MR) on the open set ℝ^P ∖ spt Q₀ and (VO), μ(ℝ^P ∖ spt Q₀) = M_{ℝ^P∖spt Q₀}(Q₀) = 0, hence μ(ℝ^P ∖ L_n) = 0; and μ(L_{n−1}) = 0 as Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0. Thus Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_FF̆) = 0 (θ ≥ 1 on M). Let 𝔉 := {F : F̆ ∩ spt Q₀ ≠ ∅}. Since spt Q₀ ⊆ K is compact, 𝔉 is finite; every F ∈ 𝔉 lies in cthickening(√n, spt Q₀) ⊆ cthickening(√P, K) (so 𝔉 ⊆ 𝔉_K); and μ(F̆) = 0 for F ∉ 𝔉. For F ∈ 𝔉, (IMC)(b) with E := F̆ (Borel) gives a current A_F represented by R_F := (M ∩ F̆, θ, ξ) (the parent's Q₀⌞F̆). For every test form ω, θξ(ω) is Hⁿ-integrable on M (|ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ ‖ω‖ a.e. by (IMC)(d), ∫_Mθ dHⁿ = M(Q₀) < ∞). Splitting the representing integral over the disjoint sets M ∩ F̆ (F ∈ 𝔉) and the Hⁿ-null remainder gives Q₀(ω) = Σ_{F∈𝔉}A_F(ω) for all ω, and M(Q₀) = Σ_{F∈𝔉}μ(F̆).

4. Orientation on faces (parent E7(a); Simon (26)). Fix F ∈ 𝔉. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ F̆ there is Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ F̆) x Q_x and ξ(x) a unit orientation of Q_x (R_F is an IMRep). Since M ∩ F̆ ⊆ Π_F ∋ x, blowUpMap x r '' (M ∩ F̆) ⊆ V_F for all r > 0. Suppose Q_x ≠ V_F; pick q ∈ Q_x ∖ V_F, ε := dist(q, V_F)/2 and f(y) := max(0, ε − |y − q|) ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Then ∫_{blowUpMap x r''(M∩F̆)}f dHⁿ = 0 for all r, while ∫_{Q_x}f dHⁿ ≥ (ε/2)Hⁿ(Q_x ∩ B_{ε/2}(q)) > 0, contradicting the definition. So Q_x = V_F and, since two unit orientations of one n-plane differ by a sign (the transition matrix between two orthonormal bases of V_F is orthogonal, with determinant ±1), ξ(x) = ±e_F. Let α_F be the n-covector α_F(v_1,…,v_n) := det((v_j)_{i_k})_{j,k}, so e_F(α_F) = 1, and s_F(x) := ξ(x)(α_F) (a.e. ±1). Define u_F := s_Fθ on {x ∈ M ∩ F̆ : s_F(x) ∈ {±1}} and u_F := 0 elsewhere; it is integer-valued on all of ℝ^P and Hⁿ-a.e. equal to 1_{M∩F̆}·θ·ξ(·)(α_F), hence a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞Π_F (Mathlib aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff; one may also first modify ξ on an Hⁿ⌞M-null set to make it Borel). Then A_F(ω) = ∫_{F̆}u_F⟨ω, e_F⟩ dHⁿ and ∫_{F̆}|u_F| dHⁿ = μ(F̆). With ũ_F := u_F ∘ φ_F (integer-valued on ℝⁿ; integrable on Q₁ with ∫_{Q₁}|ũ_F| = μ(F̆), transporting through Hⁿ⌞Π_F = (φ_F)_*Lⁿ, Mathlib Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume): A_F(ω) = ∫_{Q₁}ũ_F(y)ω(φ_Fy)(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_n}) dy.

5. Boundary variation on a face (parent E7(b); Simon (27)–(33)). For F ∈ 𝔉 let Var_F := M_{N_F}(∂Q₀) ≤ M(∂Q₀) < ∞. Claim: ∫_{Q₁}ũ_F div g ≤ Var_F for every smooth g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support in Q₁ and |g| ≤ 1.
 Let ε_j := (−1)^{j−1}dx^{i_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^{i_{j−1}} ∧ dx^{i_{j+1}} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^{i_n}. Choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(N_F), 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, with χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of the compact set φ_F(spt g) ⊆ F̆ ⊆ N_F, and put γ(x) := χ(x)Σ_jg_j(p̃_Fx)ε_j. Then γ is a test (n−1)-form with tsupport γ ⊆ N_F and |γ(x)| = χ(x)|g(p̃_Fx)| ≤ 1 (the ε_j are distinct coordinate covectors up to sign). For x ∈ F̆, ⟨dγ(x), e_F⟩ = Σ_j∂_{i_j}(χ·g_j ∘ p̃_F)(x) = div g(p̃_Fx): near points where g ∘ p̃_F ≠ 0, χ = 1; elsewhere both sides vanish; and derivatives in directions k ∉ I do not pair with e_F (dx^{i_j} ∧ ε_j = dx^{i_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^{i_n}). For G ∈ 𝔉, G ≠ F, the integrand of A_G(dγ) vanishes, because tsupport dγ ⊆ N_F and N_F ∩ Ğ ⊆ N_F ∩ L_n ∩ Ğ ⊆ F̆ ∩ Ğ = ∅. Hence ∂Q₀(γ) = Q₀(dγ) = A_F(dγ) = ∫_{Q₁}ũ_F div g, and since γ is admissible for M_{N_F}(∂Q₀), ∫_{Q₁}ũ_F div g ≤ Var_F.
 Moreover Σ_{F∈𝔉}Var_F ≤ M(∂Q₀) (parent: "the F̆ are disjoint"): for ε > 0 choose admissible γ_F with tsupport γ_F ⊆ N_F and ∂Q₀(γ_F) ≥ Var_F − ε; since the N_F are pairwise disjoint, Σ_Fγ_F is admissible (at each point at most one term is nonzero), so M(∂Q₀) ≥ Σ_FVar_F − |𝔉|ε.

6. Integer medians (parent E7(c); CB). For F ∈ 𝔉 apply CB to ũ_F and the real number V := Var_F (finite as Var_F ≤ M(∂Q₀) < ∞; CB's hypothesis is the claim of 5). There is β_F ∈ ℤ with (1) ∫_{Q₁}|ũ_F − β_F| ≤ c_BVar_F, (2) |β_F| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|ũ_F| = 2μ(F̆), and (3) |∫_{Q₁}(ũ_F − β_F)div G| ≤ c_BVar_F for every smooth G : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with |G| ≤ 1. Put β_F := 0 for F ∉ 𝔉.

7. The polyhedral current (parent E7(d); Simon (34)–(37)). Pc := Σ_{F∈𝔉}β_F[[F]]. Σ_F|β_F| ≤ 2Σ_Fμ(F̆) = 2M(Q₀) ≤ 2Λ and 𝔉 ⊆ 𝔉_K, so Pc ∈ 𝒬₀ (coefficients 0 on 𝔉_K ∖ 𝔉). Since Hⁿ(F ∖ F̆) = 0,
 (Q₀ − Pc)(ω) = Σ_{F∈𝔉}∫_{Q₁}(ũ_F − β_F)(y)ω(φ_Fy)(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_n}) dy.
 (34a) For admissible ω, |ω(x)(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_n})| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1 (one coefficient), so M(Q₀ − Pc) ≤ Σ_F∫|ũ_F − β_F| ≤ c_BΣ_FVar_F ≤ c_BM(∂Q₀).
 (34b) For an admissible (n−1)-form γ', let G_F(y)_j := (−1)^{j−1}γ'(φ_Fy)(e_{i_1},…,ê_{i_j},…,e_{i_n}). G_F is smooth and |G_F(y)|² ≤ |γ'(φ_Fy)|² ≤ 1 (distinct coefficients of γ'). By the coordinate formula for d (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_apply) and the chain rule, dγ'(φ_Fy)(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_n}) = div G_F(y). Hence ∂(Q₀ − Pc)(γ') = (Q₀ − Pc)(dγ') = Σ_F∫_{Q₁}(ũ_F − β_F)div G_F, which has absolute value ≤ c_BΣ_FVar_F ≤ c_BM(∂Q₀) by (3). So M(∂(Q₀ − Pc)) ≤ c_BM(∂Q₀).
 (36), (37) M(Pc) ≤ Σ_F|β_F| ≤ 2M(Q₀) (indeed M(Pc) = Σ|β_F|, see 8). ∂Pc = ∂Q₀ − ∂(Q₀ − Pc), so M(∂Pc) ≤ (1 + c_B)M(∂Q₀).

8. Integrality and the mass dichotomy (parent E7(e)). Pc is represented by the IMRep with carrier C_P := ⋃_{β_F≠0}F̆ (Borel, and countably n-rectifiable as a finite union of subsets of the affine images φ_F(ℝⁿ)), multiplicity |β_F| on F̆ (the F̆ are disjoint) and orientation sign(β_F)e_F. Approximate tangent space: for x ∈ F̆ and δ < δ_F(x), Π_F ∩ B_δ(x) ⊆ F̆ (points of Π_F within δ_F(x) of x have their free coordinates strictly inside (b_i, b_i + 1)), and by Lemma 2.1 no other open face meets B_δ(x); so C_P ∩ B_δ(x) = Π_F ∩ B_δ(x), and for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_ρ(0) and r < δ/ρ, ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' C_P}f dHⁿ = ∫_{V_F}f dHⁿ: V_F is the approximate tangent space, oriented by sign(β_F)e_F. The action is Σ_F∫_{F̆}|β_F|sign(β_F)⟨ω, e_F⟩ dHⁿ = Pc(ω). By (MR), M(Pc) = Σ_F|β_F|Hⁿ(F̆) = Σ_F|β_F|; hence either all β_F = 0 and Pc = 0, or M(Pc) ≥ 1.
 Boundary: for an (n−1)-form γ, Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus on [0,1]ⁿ give [[F]](dγ) = Σ_j(−1)^{j−1}([[G_j^1]](γ) − [[G_j^0]](γ)), where G_j^ε is the (n−1)-face of F with x_{i_j} = b_{i_j} + ε and [[G]](γ) := ∫_G⟨γ, e_G⟩ dH^{n−1} with its coordinate orientation e_G (for n = 1, [[G]](γ) = γ(v) at the vertex G = {v}). So ∂Pc = Σ_Gγ_G[[G]], a finite sum over (n−1)-faces with γ_G ∈ ℤ; it is integer multiplicity by the same construction in degree n − 1 (Lemma 2.1 for (n−1)-faces; for n − 1 = 0: finite carrier of vertices, multiplicity |γ_v|, orientation sign(γ_v), approximate tangent space {0} at isolated points, H⁰ the counting measure).

9. Supports (parent E7(e)).
 - spt Pc ⊆ ⋃_{β_F≠0}F. β_F ≠ 0 gives F ∈ 𝔉 (μ(F̆) ≥ |β_F|/2 > 0 by (2)), so F̆ meets spt Q₀ and F ⊆ cthickening(√n, spt Q₀) ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt Q₀).
 - spt(Q₀ − Pc) ⊆ ⋃{F ∈ 𝔉 : ∫_{Q₁}|ũ_F − β_F| > 0}. For such F, (1) gives Var_F = M_{N_F}(∂Q₀) > 0, so some γ with tsupport γ ⊆ N_F has ∂Q₀(γ) ≠ 0; by (VO), N_F meets spt ∂Q₀. As spt ∂Q₀ ⊆ spt Q₀ ⊆ L_n and N_F ∩ L_n ⊆ F̆, F̆ meets spt ∂Q₀ and F ⊆ cthickening(√n, spt ∂Q₀). Hence spt(Q₀ − Pc) ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂Q₀).
 - spt ∂Pc ⊆ spt ∂Q₀ ∪ spt ∂(Q₀ − Pc) ⊆ spt ∂Q₀ ∪ spt(Q₀ − Pc) ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂Q₀).

10. With c = max(2, 1 + c_B) ≥ 1 and the finite set 𝒬₀ of 2 (fixed before Q₀), Pc satisfies every conclusion: Pc ∈ 𝒬₀ (7), Pc and ∂Pc integer multiplicity (8), Pc = 0 or M(Pc) ≥ 1 (8), the mass bounds M(Pc) ≤ 2M(Q₀), M(∂Pc) ≤ (1 + c_B)M(∂Q₀), M(Q₀ − Pc) ≤ c_BM(∂Q₀) (7), and the support inclusions (9). ∎
proof_key_steps: Trivial case n > P; unit-grid n-faces, face currents [[F]], and the finite family of integer chains on faces in cthickening(√P, K) with Σ|β_F| ≤ 2Λ.
Pairwise disjoint open neighbourhoods N_F with N_F ∩ L_n ⊆ F̆ (distance lemma for distinct faces).
Q₀ = Σ_F Q₀⌞F̆ (MR, VO, Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0, IMC(b)); approximate tangent planes of subsets of Π_F are V_F, so Q₀⌞F̆ = ũ_F[[F̆]] with integer ũ_F.
Testing ∂Q₀ with forms built from fields g on the face gives ∫ũ_F div g ≤ Var_F := M_{N_F}(∂Q₀), and Σ_F Var_F ≤ M(∂Q₀).
CB yields integer medians β_F; Pc := Σβ_F[[F]] ∈ 𝒬₀ with M(Q₀ − Pc), M(∂(Q₀ − Pc)) ≤ c_B M(∂Q₀), M(Pc) ≤ 2M(Q₀), M(∂Pc) ≤ (1 + c_B)M(∂Q₀).
IMReps of Pc and ∂Pc (Stokes on cubes), M(Pc) = Σ|β_F| so Pc = 0 or M(Pc) ≥ 1; supports via spt Q₀ and Var_F > 0 ⇒ F̆ meets spt ∂Q₀.

The bounded integer coefficient family is finite and chosen before Q₀. subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Parts A (A1–A4) and B (B1–B5) of the parent proof with the multilinear facts (L0)–(L3) (Simon Ch. 6, 2.17–2.29 and 3.3–3.9: product with [[0,1]], homotopy formula and mass estimate, Lipschitz push-forward, integrality of push-forwards), packaged as two operators. Differences from the parent's text, all needed only for the packaging used by the sibling dimred_mbl_dt_skeleton_deformation:
 - A4(f) of the parent assumes G − F bounded; here a compactly supported cut-off χ in the straight-line homotopy removes that assumption (only [0,1] × spt X matters, as the parent notes);
 - B3 is used with O = ℝ^P and globally Lipschitz F only (the case B4 needs). The parent's application of B3 to the locally Lipschitz ψ on ℝ^P ∖ L*(a) in E4 is replaced in the sibling dimred_mbl_dt_skeleton_deformation by summing the integer multiplicity shell contributions with the sibling dimred_mbl_dt_im_series (IMS), so B1's refinement clause for an open set O and B4's parametrization-independence remark are not needed;
 - the closing combination step of B3 is the sibling IMS;
 - Part C below defines the two operators and checks the six conjuncts.

Conventions. (VO), (MR), (REP), (IMC) are the four displayed hypotheses of the statement. IMS is the sibling theorem dimred_mbl_dt_im_series, applied to (VO), (MR), (IMC). Currents are on univ in some ℝ^N = Euclid N; 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) are k-currents and 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) test k-forms. |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector, ‖ω‖ := sup_x|ω(x)|, and for a k-vector ζ (a continuous linear functional on k-covectors) |ζ| := sup{ζ(α) : |α| ≤ 1}. NC_k(ℝ^N) is the set of X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with compact support, M(X) < ∞ and, if k ≥ 1, M(∂X) < ∞ (the statement's hypothesis IsCompact X.support, X.mass < ∞, boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞). NC is closed under differences: spt(X − Y) ⊆ spt X ∪ spt Y, M(X − Y) ≤ M(X) + M(Y), and for degree ≥ 1, ∂(X − Y) = ∂X − ∂Y (GeometricCurrentOn.ext) and M(∂(X − Y)) ≤ M(∂X) + M(∂Y) (directly from the definitions). |X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖ for every current (for ε > 0, ±ω/(‖ω‖ + ε) is admissible, so ±X(ω) ≤ (‖ω‖ + ε)M(X); let ε ↓ 0). The zero current is integer multiplicity (empty carrier, multiplicity 0, orientation 0). If ω_j → 0 in the test-form topology then ‖ω_j‖ → 0 (the 0-th derivatives converge uniformly), so a linear functional bounded by a multiple of ‖·‖ is a current.

1. Multilinear algebra (parent (L0)–(L3)).
(L0) For a k-covector β, k!|β|² = Σ_{i_1,…,i_k}β(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_k})² =: ‖β‖²_HS (each increasing tuple occurs k! times up to sign, tuples with repeats vanish). ‖·‖_HS is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm of the multilinear form, hence invariant under orthogonal changes of basis, and so are |·| and the dual norm on k-vectors.
(L1) For linear A : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} and a k-covector β on ℝ^{N'}, |A^#β| ≤ ‖A‖^k|β|; dually |Λ_kAζ| ≤ ‖A‖^k|ζ|, where ⟨β, Λ_kAζ⟩ := ⟨A^#β, ζ⟩. By (L0) it suffices to bound ‖·‖_HS; replacing one slot of a multilinear form γ by A multiplies its HS norm by at most ‖A‖ (for fixed other arguments Σ_iγ(Ae_i, …)² = |Aᵀg|² ≤ ‖A‖²|g|², g the vector representing γ(·, …)); do this k times.
(L2) For a 1-covector β' and a k-covector γ, |β' ∧ γ| ≤ |β'||γ| (rotate so that β' = |β'|e¹ and use (L0)); likewise |ι_vβ| ≤ |v||β|, so |v ∧ ζ| ≤ |v||ζ| for a vector v and a k-vector ζ, where ⟨β, v ∧ ζ⟩ := ⟨ι_vβ, ζ⟩.
(L3) If τ_1,…,τ_k are orthonormal then ζ := τ_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_k (⟨α, ζ⟩ := α(τ_1,…,τ_k)) has |ζ| = 1. If A : ℝᵏ → ℝ^N is linear and injective, A = OS (S := (AᵀA)^{1/2}, O := AS^{−1} an isometric embedding), so Λ_kA(e_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ e_k) = det(S)·Oe_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ Oe_k, |Λ_kA(e)| = √det(AᵀA) =: JA, and Λ_kA(e)/JA is a unit simple k-vector orienting A(ℝᵏ). If A is not injective, Λ_kA(e) = 0 = JA. Two unit simple k-vectors orienting the same k-plane differ by a sign (the change of orthonormal basis has determinant ±1). By (IMC)(d), the orientation ξ of an IMRep satisfies |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e.

Part A. Normal currents with compact support.

2. A0 (Representation; parent "Conventions"). Let X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) have compact support and M(X) < ∞. (REP) with U = univ gives a Borel measure μ_X and ξ_X with μ_X(W) = M_W(X) for open W, |ξ_X(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, and X(ω) = ∫ξ_X(ω) dμ_X. Then μ_X(ℝ^N) = M(X) < ∞, and μ_X(ℝ^N ∖ spt X) = M_{ℝ^N∖spt X}(X) = 0 because every admissible ω supported in the open set ℝ^N ∖ spt X has X(ω) = 0 by (VO). Hence |X(ω)| ≤ ∫|ω| dμ_X, and X(ω) = 0 whenever ω vanishes on spt X.

3. A1 (Smooth push-forward). Let X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) have compact support and F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} be C^∞. For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}) put (F^#ω)(x) := ω(F(x)) ∘ DF(x) (Lean: (ω (F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x)), a smooth k-form, and F_#X(ω) := X(ζF^#ω) for ζ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^N) equal to 1 on a neighbourhood of spt X; this does not depend on ζ (two choices differ by a form vanishing near spt X; (VO)).
 - F_#X is a current. Below A1 is only applied to currents X of finite mass, and then this follows from the bound |F_#X(ω)| ≤ sup_{spt X}‖DF‖^kM(X)‖ω‖ of the last bullet and the criterion in the Conventions (in general it follows from the chain and Leibniz rules: if ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}) then ζF^#ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^k(ℝ^N), all derivatives of F being bounded on spt ζ).
 - ∂F_#X = F_#∂X: d commutes with F^# (SimonGMT exteriorDerivativeOn_pullbackFormWithin with U = V = univ), so ∂F_#X(ω) = X(ζd(F^#ω)) = X(d(ζF^#ω)) − X(dζ ∧ F^#ω). The last term vanishes by (VO) since dζ = 0 near spt X, and X(d(ζF^#ω)) = ∂X(ζF^#ω) = F_#∂X(ω) (ζ = 1 near spt ∂X ⊆ spt X).
 - spt F_#X ⊆ F(spt X): if tsupport ω ∩ F(spt X) = ∅, then F^#ω vanishes on the open set F^{-1}(ℝ^{N'} ∖ tsupport ω) ⊇ spt X, so tsupport(ζF^#ω) ∩ spt X = ∅ and F_#X(ω) = 0 by (VO). F(spt X) is compact, and a current vanishing on all forms supported in the complement of a closed set E has support in E (each point outside E has a ball with compact closure disjoint from E).
 - If M(X) < ∞, A0 gives F_#X(ω) = ∫⟨ω(F(x)), Λ_kDF(x)ξ_X(x)⟩ dμ_X(x). Hence by (L1), |F_#X(ω)| ≤ ∫‖DF‖^k|ω∘F| dμ_X and M(F_#X) ≤ sup_{spt X}‖DF‖^kM(X).

4. A2 (Product with [[0,1]]). Work directly in ℝ^{N+1} = Euclid (N + 1), writing its points as (t, x) with t the coordinate of index 0 and x ∈ ℝ^N the remaining ones (a linear isometry ℝ × ℝ^N ≅ ℝ^{N+1}, so no transport of currents is needed); e₀ := ∂_t, ι(v) := (0, v) (v ∈ ℝ^N), π(t, x) := x, i_s(x) := (s, x). For a (k+1)-form ω on ℝ^{N+1} let ω₁(t,x) be the k-covector v ↦ ω(t,x)(e₀, ιv_1,…,ιv_k) on ℝ^N, and ω₀ := ω − dt ∧ π^#ω₁ (dt-free; its restriction to ι-vectors at (t, x) is (i_t^#ω)(x)). For each fixed t, ω₁(t,·) is a test k-form on ℝ^N (smooth, support in the projection of tsupport ω). For X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with compact support and M(X) < ∞ (the only case used below) put
